trip_title: Tokyo → Kyoto Food + Culture + Anime/Tech (Relaxed 5-Day Plan, Dec 1–5)
summary: A relaxed 3-day Tokyo base followed by 2 days in Kyoto, centered on food (street food, ramen, izakayas), temples and traditional culture, plus anime/tech and photography spots. Transport is kept budget-friendly, and the user’s EUR 800 covers everything except already-booked flights and accommodation.

days.title: Arrival + Asakusa (old Tokyo)
days.morning: Check in / drop bags. Walk around Asakusa at an easy, scenic pace.
days.afternoon: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise-dori; browse small shops.
days.evening: Street-food snack run around Asakusa; izakaya dinner nearby.

days.title: Meiji Jingu + Shibuya/Harajuku anime/tech vibes
days.morning: Early visit to Meiji Jingu; short walk toward Harajuku side streets.
days.afternoon: Explore Shibuya area (Shibuya Scramble and photo spots) and enjoy anime/tech neighborhoods and shops at a relaxed pace.
days.evening: Ramen dinner; optionally a themed café or arcade for the anime/tech mood.

days.title: Tsukiji Outer Market + Akihabara
days.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market early for breakfast bites and small tastings.
days.afternoon: Akihabara for anime and tech; browse and take photos of storefronts/streets.
days.evening: Izakaya (choose another food variety vs. Day 2—order a few standout dishes and keep it light).

days.title: Travel to Kyoto + Fushimi Inari at night
days.morning: Travel Tokyo → Kyoto. Light lunch near the first Kyoto stop.
days.afternoon: Fushimi Inari Taisha for torii gates and photography; keep the pace relaxed.
days.evening: Explore Gion and nearby traditional lanes; dinner in Kyoto (izakaya or a casual traditional meal).

days.title: Temples + traditional culture + final photos
days.morning: Kiyomizu-dera area for temple + historic-street atmosphere and viewpoints.
days.afternoon: Second traditional culture stop at a relaxed pace (choose based on what still feels best after morning).
days.evening: Final meal in Kyoto: farewell dinner with street-food-style snacks and/or ramen/izakaya.

tips: Use an IC card for local convenience and keep transport economical.
Prioritize photo spots and temple areas earlier in the day for better light and fewer crowds.
For izakayas, order a few signature dishes plus one drink to keep costs controlled while still feeling like an experience.
Bundle neighborhoods within each city day to reduce unnecessary transit.
savings_tips: Start early for markets/temples and schedule photo-focused spots in daylight.
Do snacks/market tastings midday, and reserve bigger spending for ramen/izakaya dinners.
Limit paid ticketed attractions to 1–2 per day and rely on free temple-area exploration and walking.
